occurrences.quote_span: Fifteen US states sued agrichemicals company Corteva (CTVA.N) on Thursday, alleging that the spinoff of its seed and genetics business into Vylor (VYLR.N) was designed to shield the company's best assets from tens of billions of dollars in potential liabilities tied to PFAS "forever chemicals" that have polluted the environment.
occurrences.speaker: Fifteen US states

occurrences.checkable_against: Indiana state court complaint
occurrences.quote_span: The states allege that the Vylor spinoff transferred one of Corteva's most profitable businesses to a new company while leaving PFAS liabilities behind, amounting to an effort to defraud creditors pursuing claims against former DuPont entities.

occurrences.checkable_against: John Formella's statement on the Corteva-Vylor lawsuit
occurrences.quote_span: “Companies cannot simply move valuable assets out of reach and leave states, communities and taxpayers to deal with the liabilities left behind,” New Hampshire Attorney General John Formella said Thursday.

occurrences.subject: Fifteen US states' lawsuit challenging Corteva's Vylor spinoff
